title: Iman Gadzhi on agencies as a stepping stone, boring businesses, and asymmetric bets
summary: Iman Gadzhi explains why a boring agency is the best first business: low downside, free cash flow, and leverage through hiring. He covers asymmetric bets, building the team before chasing lifestyle, and treating NFTs as a pricing model for memberships. He also says wealth normalizes rather than fulfills.

principles.text: Use an agency as a stepping stone: it runs on leverage and throws off free cash flow.
principles.quote: an agency all an agency is is using leverage you're hiring people whether that's at first on a contract or per client per month basis or eventually hiring people full time to then deliver the services for you

principles.text: Start with a business where you can fail cheaply: big upside, minimal downside.
principles.quote: you want something with as much upside with this little downside you basically almost want to be you know bowling with the with the bumpers on the side right

principles.text: Seek asymmetric returns: keep making bets with large upside and near-zero downside.
principles.quote: you're looking for asymmetric returns how can i have you know a lot of upside with almost zero uh zero to no downside

principles.text: Be practical, not sexy: a boring business funds whatever life you want.
principles.quote: make your business practical and then your life can be whatever you want it to be

principles.text: Build the team and infrastructure first; if you are the weak link you cannot live like a rockstar.
principles.quote: the reason that i can live like a rockstar is because i have i built that infrastructure and i have the team

principles.text: Treat NFTs as a pricing model: charge upfront, take royalties on resale, and make a membership seat an asset.
principles.quote: for me nft is just a uh pricing model right it's it's a pricing model where you decided hey i'm gonna charge more up front than potentially i would uh you know if it was recurring or whatever
